title: Longer family interview
intro: Say: "Think about what they were like 10 years ago and compare it with what they are like now. For each situation, tell me whether they have improved, stayed the same, or got worse." The comparison is always with their own earlier level, not with other people.

source.citation: Jorm AF. A short form of the Informant Questionnaire on Cognitive Decline in the Elderly (IQCODE): development and cross-validation. Psychol Med 1994;24(1):145-153.

licence: The published form states: "There is no copyright on the Short IQCODE." The author asks to be kept informed of research projects that use it.

items.prompt: Remembering things about family and friends, such as occupations, birthdays, addresses
Remembering things that have happened recently
Recalling conversations a few days later
Remembering their own address and telephone number
Remembering what day and month it is
Remembering where things are usually kept
Remembering where to find things which have been put in a different place from usual
Knowing how to work familiar machines around the house
Learning to use a new gadget or machine around the house
Following a story in a book or on TV
Handling financial matters, such as the pension or dealing with the bank
Handling other everyday arithmetic problems, such as knowing how much food to buy or how long it is between visits from family or friends
Using their intelligence to understand what is going on and to reason things through
